Flowise CSV Agent prompt-injection: validator-bypass Python tokens POSTed to /api/v1/prediction AIDelivery Medium
Hunts unauthenticated POSTs to the Flowise CSV Agent prediction endpoint whose request body carries the pyodide blocklist-bypass constructs from CVE-2026-70477 (MRO traversal, frame inspection, __import__ reconstruction). Fires on the delivery of the injection payload before code executes. Rationale: Uses the exact validator-bypass identifiers from the CVE-2026-70477 bypass table (`__subclasses__`, `__mro__`, `__build_class__`, `gi_frame`, `f_builtins`, `BuiltinImporter.load_module`, `__import__`) which are near-nonexistent in legitimate pandas DataFrame questions, plus the confirmed unauthenticated `POST /api/v1/prediction/:id` vector. Body-capture-dependent, so scoped as hunting. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/flowise-components/CVE-2026-70477/ • https://www.elttam.com/blog/cruising-for-shells-in-flowise • https://docs.flowiseai.com/using-flowise/prediction
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006
Data sourcesWeb.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate data-science chatflow where a user genuinely asks a question containing the word `query` or pandas dunder attributes
  • Internal pentest / vulnerability scanner probing the Flowise instance post-patch
  • WAF that logs only headers/URI (no body) — produces false negatives, not false positives, but analysts may misread absence as clean
  • Security researcher replaying the public PoC in a sanctioned test tenant
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body from the WAF/proxy for the flagged /api/v1/prediction hit and confirm it contains reconstructed `__import__`/`__subclasses__` chains rather than benign pandas. Note SourceIP and whether the request was authenticated. 2) Contain: block the SourceIP at the edge and take the Flowise instance offline or upgrade to >=3.1.3 (CSVAgent removed); if unauthenticated exposure confirmed, treat as compromised. 3) Hunt: pivot to the Flowise host EDR and check for `node`-spawned shells (UC2) and outbound connections from interpreters (UC3) within minutes of this request.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/api/v1/prediction/"
| where (isempty(RequestMethod) or RequestMethod =~ "POST")
// bypass constructs live in the POST body; matched here only where the WAF forwards body content into Message / RequestURL
| where RequestURL has_any ("__subclasses__","__mro__","__build_class__","gi_frame","f_builtins","BuiltinImporter","load_module","__import__","__getattribute__")
     or Message has_any ("__subclasses__","__mro__","__build_class__","gi_frame","f_builtins","f_globals","__loader__","BuiltinImporter","load_module","__import__","__getattribute__")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, Message, DeviceProduct, RequestClientApplication
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Flowise (node) process spawning a shell — CVE-2026-70477 pyodide→child_process RCE landing AIExploitation High
Detects the Flowise Node.js process spawning an OS shell, the on-host artifact of the CVE-2026-70477 CSV Agent RCE where pyodide's JS bridge reaches Node's child_process to run attacker commands. A patched, benign Flowise never shells out from the CSV Agent, making node→shell on a Flowise host high-fidelity. Rationale: Anchored on the confirmed RCE mechanism (pyodide JS bridge → Node child_process → shell) and the Flowise-specific `node ... flowise` parent command line; a legitimate CSV Agent runs pandas inside in-process WASM and never spawns an OS shell, so this is a clean true-positive signal. Datadog left empty because its auditd schema exposes no parent-process attribute to assert the `node`/`flowise` ancestry. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elttam.com/blog/cruising-for-shells-in-flowise • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/flowise-components/CVE-2026-70477/ • https://docs.flowiseai.com/using-flowise/prediction
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.006 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • pm2 or other node-based process manager running a lifecycle/deploy hook that shells out
  • npm/yarn postinstall scripts executing under node spawning sh during a Flowise upgrade
  • Container entrypoint wrapper where node invokes a shell healthcheck
  • A deliberately-configured Flowise custom tool / 'Execute Flow' node that legitimately runs shell commands by design
  • Ops automation restarting the service via a node-driven wrapper
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pm2","npm","yarn","/usr/lib/node_modules/npm","HEALTHCHECK","entrypoint") )
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the child ProcessCommandLine — attacker commands (id, whoami, curl, /dev/tcp, base64) confirm RCE; a routine deploy/healthcheck string does not. Confirm the host runs Flowise <3.1.3. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the node process tree, and rotate any credentials/API keys the service account could read (Flowise DB, LLM provider keys). 3) Hunt: review preceding /api/v1/prediction POSTs (UC1) for the injection payload and outbound connections from node-descended interpreters (UC3); check for new cron/systemd persistence written by the shell.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "flowise"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, ProcessId
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "node"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has "flowise"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/zsh") or ActingProcessName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reverse shell / egress from Flowise node-spawned interpreter (CVE-2026-70477 post-exploit) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects an interpreter or transfer tool (bash/python/nc/socat/curl/wget) spawned under the Flowise Node.js process making an outbound connection to a public IP — the reverse-shell and exfil stage the PoC exposes via its --r_host/--r_port/--cmd options after CSV Agent RCE. Rationale: Targets the PoC's reverse-shell/exec surface (--r_host/--r_port/--l_port/--cmd) by keying on interpreters spawned by the Flowise `node` parent that either connect to a public IP (Defender network telemetry) or carry classic reverse-shell command lines (/dev/tcp, pty.spawn, -e /bin/sh). Distinct network pivot from UC2's process-spawn logic. Datadog/Sigma omitted: the required parent-process ancestry plus network correlation isn't expressible on the available Datadog auditd schema or a single-event Sigma shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.elttam.com/blog/cruising-for-shells-in-flowise • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/flowise-components/CVE-2026-70477/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A Flowise HTTP/webhook tool node legitimately fetching an external URL via curl/wget under node
  • Monitoring/APM agent whose collector is launched by node making outbound telemetry connections
  • Node-driven deploy script that curls artifacts from an internet package mirror
  • Chatflow that shells out to an approved external API as part of a sanctioned custom tool
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP != "" and not (RemoteUrl has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org","github.com","objects.githubusercontent.com"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the interpreter's command line and RemoteIP/RemotePort — a listener callback (matching a recently-seen external IP) or /dev/tcp redirection confirms a reverse shell; a known package mirror is benign. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the node process tree, and firewall the destination IP; rotate the service account and any secrets reachable from it. 3) Hunt: correlate with the originating /api/v1/prediction POST (UC1) and node→shell spawn (UC2) on the same host in the surrounding minutes, and sweep other Flowise instances for the same RemoteIP.

| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "node"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","python3","python","nc","ncat","socat","perl","curl","wget")
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] mshta.exe launched with inline http/https URL argument
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] mshta.exe spawning command interpreter or secondary LOLBin
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] RunMRU registry write launching mshta / URL / PowerShell (ClickFix-style user persistence) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] mshta.exe outbound connection to public host (remote HTA C2 retrieval) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
mshta.exe outbound connection to public host (remote HTA C2 retrieval) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the QNET-style chain where signed mshta.exe reaches out to attacker infrastructure to pull a second-stage payload. Fires on mshta.exe as the initiating process for any connection to a public IP — mshta has no legitimate reason to egress to the internet in most environments. Rationale: Anchored on the article's stated behaviour: 'mshta.exe process contacted an attacker-controlled URL and retrieved a second-stage payload' (Table 2 maps this to T1071.001). mshta egress to public IPs is near-zero in benign use. Corroborated by Sigma proc_creation_win_mshta_http and MITRE T1218.005. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/ • https://detection.fyi/sigmahq/sigma/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_mshta_http/ • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/techniques/mshta/
ATT&CKT1218.005 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy line-of-business apps that legitimately deploy signed internal HTA files hosted on an internal web server (would resolve to private IPs, excluded here)
  • Vendor management/monitoring agents that shell out to mshta against an on-prem console
  • Software installers that briefly invoke mshta against a vendor CDN
  • Security tooling / EDR test harnesses running atomic-red-team T1218.005 tests
Suppression filter
| where RemoteUrl !endswith ".internal.contoso.com"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the mshta InitiatingProcessCommandLine and the RemoteIP/RemoteUrl; check whether the destination is newly-registered or has any threat-intel hits, and identify the parent that launched mshta. 2) Contain: if the destination is unknown/malicious, isolate the device (Defender attack-disruption may already have) and block the IP/domain at the proxy. 3) Hunt: on the same host pivot to DeviceRegistryEvents for RunMRU writes and DeviceProcessEvents for child processes spawned by mshta within the surrounding 5 minutes; sweep the org for any other host that contacted the same RemoteIP.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "mshta.exe"

mshta.exe launched with inline http/https URL argument AIDelivery High
Hunts direct invocation of mshta.exe with a remote URL on the command line — the exact delivery primitive in the QNET incident where a malicious file caused mshta to fetch and execute a remote HTA. Complements the network UC by catching the command-line intent even when egress telemetry is missing. Rationale: Directly implements the article's delivery step (T1218.005 + T1204.002 in Table 2): mshta.exe proxying execution of attacker-controlled remote content. A remote URL on the mshta command line is one of the highest-fidelity LOLBin signatures. Matches the widely-deployed Sigma proc_creation_win_mshta_http logic. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/ • https://detection.fyi/sigmahq/sigma/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_mshta_http/ • https://research.splunk.com/endpoint/e13ceade-b673-4d34-adc4-4d9c01729753/
ATT&CKT1218.005 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Enterprise apps that legitimately package HTA UIs and pass an internal http URL (whitelist the internal host)
  • IT deployment scripts using mshta to render a remote help/onboarding page
  • Atomic Red Team / purple-team T1218.005 execution during scheduled testing
  • Rare third-party software updaters that stage content via mshta
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://helpdesk.contoso.com","https://intranet.contoso.com"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full mshta command line and the URL, and identify the parent process (was it a browser download, email client, or Explorer opening a downloaded file?). 2) Contain: block the URL/domain, quarantine the originating file if identifiable, and isolate the host if the URL is unknown/malicious. 3) Hunt: check DeviceFileEvents for the file the user opened and any payload mshta wrote to disk; look for RunMRU registry writes and mshta child processes on the same host and across the fleet contacting the same domain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","ftp://")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","ftp://")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Remotely Hosted HTA Executed via Mshta.EXE
id: c2a9d4f1-8b6e-49a3-bf27-1d0e6a3c9f52
description: Detects mshta.exe invoked with an http/https/ftp URL argument, indicating execution of a remotely hosted HTA payload (QNET incident delivery step).
references:

  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/05
tags:

  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'ftp://'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\Mshta.exe) @CommandLine:(*http\:* OR *https\:* OR *ftp\:*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\mshta\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(https?|ftp)://", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=mshta.exe (Processes.process="*http://*" OR Processes.process="*https://*" OR Processes.process="*ftp://*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=mshta.exe (Processes.process="*http://*" OR Processes.process="*https://*" OR Processes.process="*ftp://*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
RunMRU registry write launching mshta / URL / PowerShell (ClickFix-style user persistence) AIInstallation High
Hunts the RunMRU registry interaction the article flags as user-level persistence — the HKCU Run-dialog MRU key populated with a command that launches mshta, an http URL, or PowerShell. This is the classic ClickFix pattern where a user is socially engineered into pasting an attacker command into the Run box. Rationale: Implements the article's stated persistence artifact verbatim: 'Suspicious RunMRU-related registry interaction indicated attempted user-level persistence' (Table 2 -> T1112). External research confirms RunMRU (HKCU\...\Explorer\RunMRU) storing a URL/mshta/PowerShell command is the ClickFix fileless pattern. Falcon left empty: FDR AsepValueUpdate covers autostart ASEPs, not the non-autostart RunMRU key. Cross-checked against: • https://undercodetesting.com/detecting-clickfix-malware-via-runmru-registry-key-in-microsoft-defender/ • https://research.splunk.com/endpoint/e13ceade-b673-4d34-adc4-4d9c01729753/
ATT&CKT1112 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A power user or sysadmin legitimately typing a PowerShell or UNC command into the Run dialog
  • Help-desk staff pasting an internal http URL into Run to open a web resource
  • Developers launching local dev servers (http://localhost) via the Run box
  • Software that programmatically seeds RunMRU during setup (rare)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("svc-deploy","helpdesk-admin") and RegistryValueData has "http://localhost")
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the full RegistryValueData command that was written to RunMRU and determine whether a matching process (mshta/powershell) actually executed on the host afterward. 2) Contain: if the command is malicious, isolate the host and disable/notify the affected user account; capture the command as an IOC. 3) Hunt: pivot to DeviceProcessEvents for the exact command executing, and DeviceNetworkEvents for the URL contacted; sweep other users/hosts for the same RunMRU string (indicates a broader social-engineering / ClickFix campaign).
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has "Explorer\\RunMRU"
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("mshta","http","powershell",".hta","cmd /c")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has "Explorer\\RunMRU"
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("mshta","http","powershell",".hta","cmd /c")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious Command in RunMRU Registry Key (ClickFix)
id: 9d3c7b0a-2f45-4e18-8a6c-7b1e4f2a0c96

author: SOC Detection Engineering

| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

mshta.exe spawning command interpreter or secondary LOLBin AIExploitation High
Hunts the 'suspicious command execution' the article observed once the second-stage HTA ran under mshta — mshta.exe as parent of cmd/powershell/wscript/cscript/rundll32/regsvr32. A signed HTA host spawning a scripting engine is a strong post-exploitation execution signal. Rationale: Implements the article's 'suspicious command execution' and T1059 mapping (Table 2): the HTA-delivered script executed through mshta.exe, enabling follow-on commands. mshta parenting a scripting engine is rare in benign use and marks the pivot from delivery to hands-on execution. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/005/ • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/techniques/mshta/
ATT&CKT1059 T1218.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy internal HTA applications that shell out to cmd/wscript for legitimate automation
  • Software installers packaged as HTA that call regsvr32/rundll32 during setup
  • Admin diagnostic HTAs that launch PowerShell for system queries
  • Purple-team T1218.005 chains during authorized testing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "C:\\Program Files\\ContosoLOB\\app.hta")
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the child process command line (decode any base64/encoded PowerShell) and the parent mshta command line to determine what the HTA instructed. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process tree, and preserve the mshta parent and any dropped files for forensics. 3) Hunt: enumerate everything the child spawned (grandchildren), check DeviceNetworkEvents for C2 from the child, DeviceRegistryEvents for RunMRU/Run-key persistence, and DeviceFileEvents for payloads written to Temp/AppData; sweep the fleet for the same mshta->child pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "mshta.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\mshta.exe"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.

Malicious csvFile data URI with Python/JS breakout posted to Flowise /api/v1/prediction AIExploitation Medium
Hunts POST requests to Flowise's public /api/v1/prediction/<id> endpoint carrying a csvFile data URI whose base64 segment contains Python/JS breakout tokens (import js, js.eval, child_process, __import__). Distinguishes malicious CSVAgent abuse from benign base64 CSV uploads by requiring the interpreter-escape strings the exploit needs. Rationale: Uses the article-specific endpoint path /api/v1/prediction/ (WHITELIST_URLS, reachable unauthenticated) plus the exact breakout tokens the exploit interpolates (import js, js.eval, child_process, __import__, and the read_pickle variant from the sibling advisory). Request-body inspection requires WAF/proxy full-capture; Defender/Datadog/Falcon left empty as those sources do not ship HTTP bodies. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/flowise/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv/ • https://gbhackers.com/six-flowise-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate CSVAgent usage: analysts uploading a real base64-encoded CSV data URI to a prediction flow (no breakout tokens present)
  • Security scanners / DAST tools probing the prediction endpoint with test payloads
  • Internal red-team or pentest validation of CVE-2026-69264
  • WAF already blocking the request (still logged as attempt)
Suppression filter
| where not(Message has_any ("nessus","qualys","burpsuite","acunetix") or RequestClientApplication has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Burp"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body for the flagged prediction call; confirm the csvFile base64 segment decodes to Python containing js.eval / import('child_process') / read_pickle rather than legitimate CSV bytes. Note source IP and whether the chatflow has an apikeyid set (unauthenticated = higher risk). 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, disable the exposed chatflow, and confirm Flowise is patched to >=3.1.3; if pre-patch, take the instance offline. 3) Hunt: on the Flowise host, pivot to child processes of node.exe within the same window (UC2/UC3) and search for dropped files (e.g. proof.txt) or outbound C2 from the node process.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/api/v1/prediction/"
| where Message has_any ("csvFile","data:","base64,","import js","js.eval","child_process","__import__","read_pickle","u002c") or RequestContext has_any ("csvFile","js.eval","child_process","__import__")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, DeviceProduct, DeviceVendor, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Flowise Node.js process spawning shell/interpreter child (CSVAgent RCE) AIExploitation High
Hunts the Flowise node process (command line containing flowise/pyodide) spawning cmd, PowerShell, bash, sh, wsl or similar interpreters. Under normal operation Flowise never spawns an OS shell, so this parent→child pair is a direct post-exploitation artifact of the CVE-2026-69264 Pyodide js-bridge breakout. Rationale: Anchored on the article's execution primitive: Flowise (node) reaching import('child_process') and cp.execSync, which materialises as node.exe spawning an OS shell. The flowise/pyodide command-line filter scopes to the vulnerable app so the parent binary alone (node) does not over-fire. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv • https://www.cryptika.com/six-flowise-rce-flaws-let-attackers-execute-code-on-ai-workflow-servers/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Flowise Custom Function / Custom Tool node legitimately configured by an operator to shell out
  • Developer running Flowise under nodemon/npm scripts that spawn shells during hot reload
  • Container entrypoint wrappers where node execs sh for health checks
  • Legitimate use of a Flowise 'Execute Command' style community node
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("nodemon","npm-cli.js","healthcheck","docker-entrypoint"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ProcessCommandLine — recon (whoami/id/hostname), download (curl/wget), or reverse shell strongly confirm RCE; capture the parent node command line and the DeviceName. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the node process, and take the Flowise instance offline pending patch to >=3.1.3. 3) Hunt: enumerate all chatflows on the instance for CSVAgent nodes with crafted csvFile/read_pickle payloads, review /api/v1/prediction access logs for the triggering request (UC1), and check for persistence, dropped files, and outbound C2 from the node process.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise","pyodide")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","dash","wsl.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "node"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise","pyodide")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh.exe","dash","wsl.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Flowise Node Process Spawns OS Shell (CSVAgent Pyodide RCE)
id: 8a1c4e77-2b93-4d6f-9a10-5c7e2f0b1d38
description: Detects the Flowise node process spawning an OS shell or interpreter, the post-exploitation signature of CVE-2026-69264 Pyodide js-bridge breakout
references:

Flowise Node process burst-spawning shell/recon children within seconds (post-RCE) AIExploitation High
Alerts when the Flowise node process spawns two or more shell/recon interpreter children inside a 2-second window — the process-tree explosion that follows a successful CSVAgent Pyodide breakout. Uses a temporal count threshold to separate a scripted RCE chain from a single benign shell-out. Rationale: Distinct pivot from UC2: temporal count threshold on the node process. The article's PoC chains multiple OS actions (import, write, execSync); a burst of >=2 shell/recon children in 2s from a flowise-tagged node parent is far higher fidelity than a single spawn. Datadog threshold is applied at rule level. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv • https://gbhackers.com/six-flowise-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A single Flowise custom node legitimately fanning out several shell commands in a batch job
  • Node build/test tooling (npm/nodemon) that spins up parallel shells during startup
  • Container orchestration probes issuing rapid sh health checks against the node PID
  • Operator debugging the Flowise host by scripting commands through a custom tool
Suppression filter
| where not (Cmds has_any ("nodemon","docker-entrypoint","healthcheck"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the Cmds set from the bucket — presence of recon (whoami/id), egress (curl/wget) or a reverse shell confirms exploitation; record DeviceName and the node InitiatingProcessId. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the node process tree, and pull the Flowise instance until it is on >=3.1.3. 3) Hunt: correlate the burst timestamp against /api/v1/prediction access logs (UC1) to identify the source IP and chatflow, then sweep other Flowise hosts for the same node→shell burst pattern and audit chatflows for malicious CSVAgent nodes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise","pyodide")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","dash","wsl.exe","curl.exe","whoami.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ShellChildren = count(), Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, bin(Timestamp, 2s)
| where ShellChildren >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "node"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("flowise","pyodide")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh.exe","dash","wsl.exe","curl.exe","whoami.exe")
| summarize ShellChildren = count(), Cmds = make_set(TargetProcessCommandLine, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, bin(TimeGenerated, 2s)
| where ShellChildren >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE) @ParentCommandLine:(*flowise* OR *Flowise* OR *pyodide*) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\wsl.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\whoami.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|dash|wsl|curl|whoami)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=count())
| count >= 2
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Processes.process_name) as child_procs values(Processes.process) as cmds values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","node") AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","dash","wsl.exe","curl.exe","whoami.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_id _time span=2s

Flowise Node.js process spawning OS shell/recon (Pyodide js-interop RCE sink) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the terminal RCE step of CVE-2026-70470: Pyodide's js module bridge reaches process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync, causing the Flowise Node.js process to spawn a native OS shell or recon binary. On a stock Flowise host the node service never legitimately shells out to cmd.exe/sh to run id/hostname/whoami, so a node parent spawning a command interpreter is a high-fidelity exploitation signal. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact RCE sink (process.mainModule.require('child_process').execSync running 'id && hostname && echo FLOWISE_RCE_CONFIRMED') and the fact that the reachable process is Node.js (Flowise). node -> shell is anomalous on a production Flowise host; the flowise cmdline marker plus recon strings keep FP low. Cross-checked GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2 and prior CVE-2026-41264 (same Pyodide->child_process sink). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3hjv-c53m-58jj • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html • https://gbhackers.com/six-flowise-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp / npm / yarn build steps spawning cmd.exe or sh during dependency install on developer or CI hosts
  • A legitimate Flowise Custom Tool or ExecuteFlow node designed to shell out to a local script
  • Container health-check or entrypoint wrappers where a node supervisor spawns sh
  • Puppeteer / headless-chrome automation launched from a node process on the same host
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","node_modules","webpack","next dev","yarn","npm install","prebuild","puppeteer"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the child ProcessCommandLine — recon (id/whoami/hostname/uname), reverse-shell, or download strings confirm exploitation; verify the parent node cmdline is the Flowise service (contains 'flowise'), not a dev/CI build tool. 2) Contain: network-isolate the host, kill the offending node process or restart/redeploy the Flowise pod, and pull the public CSV/Airtable-Agent chatflow offline until patched to >=3.1.3. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound connections from the node process after the spawn (C2/exfil), search reverse-proxy logs for the preceding /api/v1/prediction request with homoglyph payload (UC2), and check for dropped files or new persistence written by the node process.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh","bash","dash","zsh","id","hostname","whoami","uname")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "flowise"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("FLOWISE_RCE_CONFIRMED","hostname","whoami","child_process","/etc/passwd")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\node.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("flowise","FLOWISE_RCE_CONFIRMED","hostname","whoami","child_process")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Flowise Node.js Process Spawning OS Shell (Pyodide js-interop RCE)
id: a3f1c9d2-7b64-4e18-9c2a-5e0f1b8d6a44
status: experimental
description: Detects the Flowise node process spawning a command interpreter or recon binary, the terminal RCE step of CVE-2026-70470 via Pyodide child_process.execSync.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3hjv-c53m-58jj
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/04
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.006
  - attack.t1190
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '/node'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '/sh'
      - '/bash'
      - '/dash'
      - '/id'
      - '/hostname'
      - '/whoami'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - node-based build tooling (node-gyp, webpack) spawning shells on developer or CI hosts
  - legitimate Flowise custom tool nodes that shell out
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\Cmd.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|dash|zsh|id|hostname|whoami|uname)(\.exe)?$/i
| regex("(?i)(flowise|FLOWISE_RCE_CONFIRMED|hostname|whoami|child_process|/etc/passwd)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Unicode homoglyph dunder payload to Flowise /api/v1/prediction (validator bypass) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the CVE-2026-70470 defense-evasion step: an HTTP POST to Flowise's /api/v1/prediction endpoint whose body carries Python dunder identifiers built from Mathematical Alphanumeric homoglyphs (U+1D400-U+1D7FF, e.g. __cl𝐚ss__, __b𝐮iltins__) or Cyrillic lookalikes, which slip past the ASCII \b-based validatePythonCodeForDataFrame blacklist. These characters effectively never appear in legitimate chat input, making their presence near double underscores high-signal. Rationale: Uses the article's exact bypass mechanism (Mathematical Bold homoglyphs U+1D400-U+1D7FF such as U+1D41A/U+1D42E forming __class__/__builtins__) against the named endpoint /api/v1/prediction. CIM Web tstats and Defender/Falcon EDR do not carry HTTP POST bodies, so this is expressed as a raw reverse-proxy/WAF search and Sentinel CommonSecurityLog (WAF) regex; leave defender/datadog/falcon empty as their telemetry lacks the request body. Corroborated against GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-52fh-8v99-63c2
ATT&CKT1027 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Data-science users pasting genuine mathematical notation (bold/italic Unicode math symbols) into a chat prompt
  • Russian or other Cyrillic-language chat input containing underscores
  • Copy-pasted styled text (LinkedIn/Twitter 'bold' Unicode) submitted as a chat message
  • Authorized penetration testers or vulnerability scanners probing the /api/v1/prediction endpoint
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the decoded body — confirm the homoglyph characters sit inside identifier positions adjacent to double underscores (__cl𝐚ss__, __subcl𝐚sses__, __b𝐮iltins__) rather than free prose; note the source IP and chatflowId. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, take the affected public CSV/Airtable-Agent chatflow offline, and confirm Flowise is upgraded to >=3.1.3. 3) Hunt: correlate to UC1 on the Flowise host — did the node process spawn a shell within seconds of this request? Search for other requests from the same IP/UA and any prior reconnaissance of the endpoint.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestURL has "/api/v1/prediction"
| where (Message matches regex @"[\x{1D400}-\x{1D7FF}]")
   or (RequestContext matches regex @"[\x{1D400}-\x{1D7FF}]")
   or (Message has "__" and Message matches regex @"[\x{0400}-\x{04FF}]")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
index=* sourcetype IN (flowise, nginx, nginx:plus:access, haproxy:http, aws:waf) uri_path="/api/v1/prediction*" http_method=POST
| regex _raw="[\x{1D400}-\x{1D7FF}]"
| table _time, src_ip, host, uri_path, http_user_agent, status, _raw
| sort - _time

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Flowise additionalConfig database-path override in vector-upsert API request (CVE-2026-69259) · [LLM] Flowise node runtime spawns shell interpreter (post-exploit command execution) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Flowise node process writes SQLite DB file to system directory (arbitrary-write RCE primitive) · [LLM] Flowise node process writes to cron / systemd / SSH persistence path · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-69259: Flowise RCE via SQLite Record Manager Node
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Flowise additionalConfig database-path override in vector-upsert API request (CVE-2026-69259) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP POSTs to Flowise ingestion endpoints carrying an `additionalConfig` payload that overrides the SQLite `database` path (or supplies TypeORM `entities`/`migrations` for JS-load RCE). This is the exact exploitation primitive for CVE-2026-69259 in FlowiseAI 3.1.2. Rationale: Uses the article's exact vulnerable input name `additionalConfig` reaching the Record Manager node via Flowise's `/api/v1/vector/upsert` and document-store ingestion endpoints, correlated with an out-of-tree path (`/etc/`, `/root/`, `.sqlite`) or TypeORM `entities`/`migrations` keys — the confirmed RCE vector. Body inspection requires the proxy/WAF to log request bodies. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html • https://www.securityweek.com/exploit-code-published-for-critical-flowise-rce-vulnerability/ • https://gbhackers.com/six-flowise-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate automation that passes overrideConfig/additionalConfig with a benign in-tree .flowise database path
  • Security scanners / internal pentest hitting the upsert endpoint
  • Developers testing custom Record Manager configs against a staging instance
  • Load-testing tools replaying recorded upsert requests
Suppression filter
| where not (Message has ".flowise" and Message !has_any ("/etc/", "/root/", "/var/spool/cron", "/dev/shm", "entities", "migrations"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request body for matched events; confirm whether `additionalConfig.database` (or TypeORM `entities`/`migrations`) points outside the `~/.flowise` directory to a system path. Identify the authenticated Flowise user/API key used. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF, revoke the Flowise API key, and confirm the Flowise version — upgrade 3.1.2 → 3.1.3+ immediately. 3) Hunt: on the Flowise host pivot to node file-writes and child-process spawns in the following minutes (see companion UCs) to determine if the write/RCE succeeded.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL has_any ("/api/v1/vector/upsert", "/api/v1/prediction", "/api/v1/document-store")
| where Message has "additionalConfig" or RequestURL has "additionalConfig" or RequestContext has "additionalConfig"
| where Message has_any ("database", "/etc/", "/root/", "/var/spool/cron", "entities", "migrations", ".sqlite") or RequestURL has_any ("/etc/", "/root/", ".sqlite")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, Message
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| where like(url,"%additionalConfig%") OR like(url,"%/api/v1/vector/upsert%") OR like(url,"%/api/v1/document-store%")
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Flowise node process writes SQLite DB file to system directory (arbitrary-write RCE primitive) AIInstallation High
Detects the Flowise node runtime creating a .sqlite/.sqlite3/.db file outside its `.flowise` home in a sensitive system directory — the direct file-write artifact of the CVE-2026-69259 additionalConfig database-path override, which runs as root in the flowiseai/flowise:3.1.2 Docker image. Rationale: Directly grounded in the article's statement that the flaw lets an attacker 'write an SQLite database to an arbitrary filepath, which includes system directories' while the 3.1.2 Docker image 'runs as root'. Keys on node as the writer + SQLite extension + system path, explicitly excluding the legitimate `.flowise` home. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html • https://gbhackers.com/six-flowise-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Flowise misconfigured with DATABASE_PATH pointed at a non-default but legitimate directory (e.g. /var/lib/flowise)
  • Backup jobs copying database.sqlite into /root or /var for archival
  • Container image that bind-mounts the SQLite DB to a host system path by design
  • Admin manually relocating the Flowise DB during maintenance
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !startswith "/var/lib/flowise" and FolderPath !startswith "/opt/flowise"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the FolderPath is a genuine system dir (not an approved custom DATABASE_PATH) and capture the file — a SQLite header ('SQLite format 3') in /etc or /root is exploitation. Note InitiatingProcessCommandLine and the writing UID (expect root). 2) Contain: isolate the container/host, snapshot the file for forensics, then delete the planted DB and upgrade Flowise to 3.1.3+. 3) Hunt: correlate back to the preceding upsert API request (web UC) and forward to any cron/persistence file writes or node-spawned shells to scope full RCE.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "nodejs", "node.exe")
| where FileName endswith ".sqlite" or FileName endswith ".sqlite3" or FileName endswith ".db"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/", "/root/", "/var/spool/", "/usr/local/sbin/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/dev/shm/")
| where FolderPath !contains ".flowise"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath
| sort by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where ActingProcessName has "node"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".sqlite" or TargetFileName endswith ".sqlite3" or TargetFileName endswith ".db"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/", "/root/", "/var/spool/", "/usr/local/sbin/", "/usr/local/bin/", "/dev/shm/")
| where TargetFilePath !has ".flowise"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Flowise node process writes to cron / systemd / SSH persistence path AIInstallation High
Detects the Flowise node runtime creating or modifying a file in cron, systemd, init, or SSH authorized_keys directories — the likely means of converting the CVE-2026-69259 root arbitrary-write into code execution and persistence. Rationale: The article states the write targets 'system directories' as root; the canonical way to weaponize a root arbitrary-write into RCE/persistence is dropping a crontab/systemd unit or root authorized_keys. A node process — which should only ever touch its `.flowise` dir — writing to any of these paths is near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html • https://www.securityweek.com/exploit-code-published-for-critical-flowise-rce-vulnerability/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1543.002 T1098.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A Flowise container entrypoint script legitimately templating a systemd unit or cron entry at startup (rare)
  • Configuration-management agent (Ansible/Chef) mislabeled as node writing cron files
  • Admin editing root crontab while a node debug session holds the shell
  • Backup tooling restoring /root/.ssh from a snapshot
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the written file — a cron line, systemd ExecStart, or new SSH key added by node is a confirmed persistence implant; capture the payload command/key. 2) Contain: isolate the host, remove the malicious cron/unit/key, kill the Flowise container, and rotate any credentials on the box; upgrade to 3.1.3+. 3) Hunt: enumerate all cron.d/systemd/init.d/authorized_keys entries created since the first suspicious upsert request, and check for outbound connections from the payload (node-spawned shell UC).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "nodejs")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/", "/etc/cron.daily/", "/etc/cron.hourly/", "/etc/crontab", "/var/spool/cron/", "/etc/systemd/system/", "/etc/init.d/", "/root/.ssh/")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath
| sort by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "node"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/", "/etc/cron.daily/", "/etc/cron.hourly/", "/etc/crontab", "/var/spool/cron/", "/etc/systemd/system/", "/etc/init.d/", "/root/.ssh/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Flowise node runtime spawns shell interpreter (post-exploit command execution) AIExploitation Medium
Detects the Flowise node process spawning bash/sh/dash/zsh (or cmd/powershell) — behaviour Flowise never exhibits in normal operation, indicating command execution following CVE-2026-69259 exploitation (e.g. via a TypeORM entities JS payload loaded through additionalConfig). Rationale: The advisory is titled an RCE; a normal Flowise node server does not fork interactive shells, so node -> bash/sh/powershell (especially with -c, /dev/tcp, curl/wget/nc, or base64 tokens) is a strong post-exploitation indicator. Parent-child pairing (node parent) plus suspicious-arg tokens keeps fidelity up. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html • https://www.securityweek.com/exploit-code-published-for-critical-flowise-rce-vulnerability/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A Flowise Tool/Custom-Function node that legitimately shells out (e.g. an admin-authored code-interpreter tool)
  • Container healthcheck or entrypoint wrapper invoking sh -c at startup
  • npm lifecycle scripts running sh during in-container package install/upgrade
  • Monitoring agents embedded in the image spawning sh for metric collection
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "npm" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install", "ci", "run"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect the child ProcessCommandLine — reverse-shell (/dev/tcp, nc -e), downloader (curl|wget), or base64 blob confirms exploitation; benign `sh -c` from a known custom tool node may be expected. Identify the initiating node PID and its network peers. 2) Contain: kill the child process, isolate the container/host, block any outbound C2 IP, and revoke Flowise API keys; patch to 3.1.3+. 3) Hunt: correlate with preceding upsert API requests and node file-writes (companion UCs), and sweep other Flowise hosts for the same node->shell pattern.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node", "nodejs")
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c", "/dev/tcp/", "curl ", "wget ", "nc ", " -i", "base64", "python", "/tmp/") or FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has "node"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "/sh", "dash", "zsh", "cmd.exe", "powershell", "pwsh")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c", "/dev/tcp/", "curl ", "wget ", "nc ", " -i", "base64", "python", "/tmp/") or ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe", "powershell")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)

Flowise node.js spawns Unix shell/command binaries as root (CSVAgent Pyodide RCE) AIExploitation High
Hunts the core of CVE-2026-69255: the Flowise node.js process using Pyodide's js bridge to call process.mainModule.constructor._load('child_process').execSync() and spawn OS commands as root (PID 1 in container). A node process that is a Flowise workflow engine should never fork /bin/sh, id, uname, or whoami — that child is the injected payload executing. Rationale: Grounded in the verified chain (process.mainModule.constructor._load('child_process').execSync('id') as root, PID 1). A node parent forking a shell/recon binary is the direct RCE observable; requiring AccountName=root matches the article's verified 'Server username: root'. Cross-checked GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv / CVE-2026-41264 confirming the same CSVAgent→pyodide→child_process path. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/flowise/CVE-2026-41264/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.006 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Flowise/LangChain nodes that legitimately shell out to a Python tool via a custom Tool node (env, python3)
  • Container entrypoint/health-check scripts where node is the init process invoking sh at startup
  • CI/build images where node runs as root and calls git/curl during package install
  • Admin exec-ing into the container and running id/uname for troubleshooting (parent would be sh, not node)
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("node_modules","npm","yarn","pnpm","/healthz","docker-entrypoint") and FileName in~ ("sh","bash"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the child ProcessCommandLine and the InitiatingProcessCommandLine — a raw `id`/`uname`/`sh -c` with no Flowise tool wrapper, executed as root under a node parent, is a true positive. Confirm the host runs Flowise <=3.1.2. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate/kill the container, rotate FLOWISE_PASSWORD and any API keys under /root/.flowise, and block the source IP hitting /api/v1/prediction. 3) HUNT: On the same host pivot to outbound connections from node/sh (reverse shell UC), reads of /root/.flowise and /etc/passwd, and the upstream POST /api/v1/chatflows + /api/v1/prediction requests that delivered the payload.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","id","uname","whoami","cat","env","curl","wget","python3")
| where AccountName == "root" or InitiatingProcessAccountName == "root"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("/sh","/bash","/dash","/id","/uname","/whoami","/cat","/env","/curl","/wget","/python3")
| where ActorUsername == "root" or TargetUsername == "root"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects the Flowise node process forking a Unix shell or system-recon binary, the observable behaviour of CSVAgent Pyodide code injection RCE.

  - https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^node(js)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(sh|bash|dash|id|uname|whoami|cat|env|curl|wget|python3)$/i

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","nodejs")) (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","id","uname","whoami","cat","env","curl","wget","python3")) Processes.user="root" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node","nodejs")) (Processes.process_name IN ("sh","bash","dash","id","uname","whoami","cat","env","curl","wget","python3")) Processes.user="root" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Reverse shell / Meterpreter egress from Flowise node or its shell child AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the verified Meterpreter reverse_tcp session by flagging outbound public connections initiated by the Flowise node process or a shell it spawned, on ports other than normal web/DNS. Port-agnostic (not tied to the article's 4444) so it survives operator payload changes. Rationale: Article verifies a Meterpreter session opened from the exploited node process (172.17.0.2 -> 172.17.0.1:4444). Pivoting on node/shell as the initiating process to a public IP on a non-web port catches the reverse shell without hardcoding the port. Sentinel left empty: ImNetworkSession carries no process attribution, so the node/shell parent constraint cannot be expressed on available Sentinel tables. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv • https://www.securityweek.com/exploit-code-published-for-critical-flowise-rce-vulnerability/amp/
ATT&CKT1571 T1059.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Flowise node making outbound LLM/vector-DB API calls on non-standard ports (e.g. self-hosted Ollama :11434, Qdrant :6333)
  • node connecting to a database backend (Postgres :5432, MySQL :3306)
  • Monitoring/APM agents launched by node (StatsD/OTLP ports)
  • Package registry pulls over a proxy on a custom port during container build
Suppression filter
| where RemoteIP !in ("127.0.0.1") and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs") and RemotePort in (11434, 6333, 5432, 3306, 6379))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Resolve RemoteIP ownership and reputation; a public IP with no PTR/vendor mapping reached from a freshly-spawned sh child of node is high-confidence C2. Check for a preceding node->sh spawn (UC1). 2) CONTAIN: Kill the container, blackhole the RemoteIP at the egress firewall, and capture memory if IR requires the Meterpreter stager. 3) HUNT: Search for the same RemoteIP/ASN across other Flowise hosts and for staged download commands (curl/wget) in node child command lines.
DeviceNetworkEvents

System-recon commands executed under Flowise node/shell context AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation discovery burst the PoC demonstrates (id, uname -a, cat /etc/hostname) run as children of node or a node-spawned shell. Targets both recon binaries and reads of sensitive host files that reveal container/host identity. Rationale: PoC output shows id, uname -a and cat /etc/hostname run immediately after the shell opens. Requiring a node/shell parent plus >=2 distinct recon actions distinguishes attacker enumeration from a single benign uname. /root/.flowise and /etc/passwd are the exact sensitive targets the article names. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv
ATT&CKT1082 T1033
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Container entrypoint scripts running uname/hostname to set labels
  • Health checks or app code that reads /etc/hostname for self-identification
  • Ops staff running id/whoami after exec-ing into the container
  • Backup/monitoring jobs that grep /etc/passwd for account inventory
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker-entrypoint","healthcheck","/entrypoint.sh") )
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Look at command ordering and timing — id -> uname -> cat /etc/hostname within seconds under a node-spawned shell is hands-on-keyboard recon, not a startup script. 2) CONTAIN: Snapshot then isolate the container; preserve shell history. 3) HUNT: Follow with credential-store access (UC4) and outbound C2 (UC2) from the same PID/host, and review who triggered the originating /api/v1/prediction call.

Access to Flowise credential store /root/.flowise and secret env vars AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the verified credential theft: reads of the Flowise SQLite/config store at /root/.flowise (DATABASE_PATH) and dumping of FLOWISE_PASSWORD / APIKEY_PATH secrets from a node-spawned shell. These exact strings appear in the article's post-exploitation output. Rationale: The article's 'Additional Verified Impact / Credential Theft' block names FLOWISE_PASSWORD, DATABASE_PATH=/root/.flowise and APIKEY_PATH verbatim. These are high-fidelity literals; a shell child of node referencing them is credential harvesting, not normal Flowise operation (the app reads its own DB via the node process, not via cat/grep). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate backup/migration scripts that tar or copy /root/.flowise
  • Ops staff grepping env for DATABASE_PATH during troubleshooting
  • Container entrypoint exporting FLOWISE_PASSWORD/DATABASE_PATH at startup (parent would be the init shell, not node)
  • Config-management tooling templating the Flowise env file
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker-entrypoint","/entrypoint.sh","backup","rsync","tar "))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the accessing process is a shell child of node rather than the entrypoint; a cat/grep of /root/.flowise from an interactive-looking shell is theft. 2) CONTAIN: Immediately rotate FLOWISE_PASSWORD, the SQLite DB credentials and every API key stored under /root/.flowise and APIKEY_PATH; revoke downstream tokens (OpenAI, vector DB). 3) HUNT: Check outbound transfers (UC2) that could have exfiltrated the store, and review auth logs for the leaked admin password being reused elsewhere.

| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/root/.flowise", "FLOWISE_PASSWORD", "APIKEY_PATH", "DATABASE_PATH")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs","sh","bash","dash")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/root/.flowise", "FLOWISE_PASSWORD", "APIKEY_PATH", "DATABASE_PATH")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Flowise CSVAgent exploit HTTP sequence: chatflow create + prediction trigger AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the delivery pattern for CVE-2026-69255 at the web tier: an authenticated client creating a chatflow (POST /api/v1/chatflows) then invoking it (POST /api/v1/prediction/<UUID>) — the two-request pattern every public PoC/Metasploit module uses to plant and fire the CSVAgent payload. Rationale: External corroboration (GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv, GitLab GLAD) confirms exploitation = POST /api/v1/chatflows to create the malicious CSVAgent flow, then POST /api/v1/prediction/<UUID> to execute it. Requiring both endpoints from one source in a window is the article-specific delivery fingerprint. Defender/Datadog/Falcon left empty: this is web-proxy telemetry with no clean endpoint-EDR or CloudTrail equivalent. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/FlowiseAI/Flowise/security/advisories/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv • https://advisories.gitlab.com/npm/flowise/GHSA-9wc7-mj3f-74xv/ • https://gbhackers.com/six-flowise-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Flowise builders creating and testing chatflows during normal development
  • Automated CI/CD or IaC that programmatically provisions chatflows then smoke-tests them via /prediction
  • Load-testing or synthetic-monitoring hitting the prediction API
  • A single power user rapidly iterating on a flow
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the request bodies (if the proxy captures them) and look for the CSVAgent payload markers `import js`, `child_process`, `_load`, or `execSync` and the comma-free breakout `";import js`; correlate SourceIP with an authenticated session. 2) CONTAIN: Block the source IP, force-expire the attacker's Flowise session/token, and take the instance off the internet until patched to >=3.1.3. 3) HUNT: On the Flowise host, pivot to node->shell spawns (UC1), credential-store access (UC4) and reverse-shell egress (UC2) originating shortly after the /prediction call.

| where RequestMethod == "POST"
| where RequestURL has "/api/v1/prediction/" or RequestURL has "/api/v1/chatflows"
| extend Endpoint = iff(RequestURL has "/api/v1/prediction/", "prediction", "chatflows")

Flowise/node process spawning Unix shell or netcat reverse shell (CVE-2026-69254 vm2 escape) AIInstallation High
Hunts the on-host manifestation of the CVE-2026-69254 vm2 sandbox escape: the Flowise 'node' process spawning /bin/sh, bash, nc, ncat or socat with reverse-shell markers. A node-parent-to-shell edge carrying /dev/tcp or nc -e is the highest-fidelity signal of the escape reaching child_process. Rationale: Anchored on the article's exact escape endpoint (node child_process launching a reverse shell) and the PoC's nc pattern to 172.17.0.1:1337; node-parent-to-shell with /dev/tcp or nc -e is a rare, high-fidelity edge. Cross-checked vm2-escape-to-child_process behaviour against the vm2 advisory wave and Flowise active-exploitation reporting. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-3769-jgqc-cxm7 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/vm2-nodejs-library-vulnerabilities.html • https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/flowise-ai-agent-builder-under-active.html • https://www.rapid7.com/db/modules/exploit/multi/http/flowise_js_rce/
ATT&CKT1211 T1059.004 T1059.007 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Node-based build tooling (node-gyp, prebuild, npm/yarn lifecycle scripts) forking sh -c during image builds
  • Flowise/node worker legitimately shelling out to ffmpeg/imagemagick/git via child_process for document processing
  • Container healthcheck scripts using nc to test port reachability of a downstream service
  • Developer or CI running a node app interactively that spawns bash for a subprocess helper
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild","npm ","yarn ","node_modules/.bin","/usr/bin/ffmpeg","convert ","git ")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Pull the full child ProcessCommandLine and the node parent's InitiatingProcessCommandLine; confirm the shell/nc invocation carries a reverse-shell shape (/dev/tcp, -e /bin/sh, mkfifo) and identify the remote endpoint. Check whether the host runs Flowise and is internet-reachable. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host/container, kill the node and child shell PIDs, and block the observed remote IP:port at the egress firewall. Rotate any secrets (E2B/API keys, DB creds) reachable from the Flowise process. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the node PID for outbound connections (UC2), review Flowise API/auth logs for the preceding AgentAsTool/baseURL config change, and search other Flowise hosts for the same parent-child edge.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","nodejs")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","netcat","nc.traditional","socat")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("child_process","/dev/tcp/","-e /bin/sh","-e /bin/bash","bash -i","sh -i","mkfifo")
| where FileName in~ ("nc","ncat","netcat","nc.traditional","socat")
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","-e /bin/sh","-e /bin/bash","bash -i","sh -i","mkfifo")
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild","npm ","yarn ","node_modules/.bin"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","nodejs")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","nc","ncat","netcat","socat")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("nc","ncat","netcat","socat")
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/dev/tcp/","-e /bin/sh","-e /bin/bash","bash -i","sh -i","mkfifo","child_process")
| where not(ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild","node_modules/.bin"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Flowise node process spawning shell or reverse-shell tool (CVE-2026-69254)
id: 6a1e4c9f-2b7d-4e83-9c1a-5f0d8e7b3a21
status: experimental
description: Detects the Flowise/node process spawning a Unix shell or netcat/socat carrying reverse-shell markers, consistent with the CVE-2026-69254 vm2 sandbox escape to host RCE.
references:

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/node'
      - '/nodejs'
  selection_child_tool:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/nc'
      - '/ncat'
      - '/netcat'
      - '/socat'
  selection_child_shell:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/sh'

      - '-e /bin/bash'

      - 'sh -i'
      - 'mkfifo'
  condition: selection_parent and (selection_child_tool or selection_child_shell)
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.name:(nc OR ncat OR netcat OR socat) OR @process.command_line:(*"/dev/tcp/"* OR *"-e /bin/sh"* OR *"-e /bin/bash"* OR *"bash -i"* OR *"sh -i"* OR *mkfifo*)) -@process.command_line:(*node-gyp* OR *node_modules/.bin* OR *prebuild*)
